headline: High: RD-Agent’s broad egress and browser use can leak or act on ai-engineering-hub outputs, while shared write surfaces and unverified docs leave interaction risks only partially bounded.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no documented input surfaces beyond docs, but B can run browsers and ingest web content, so if A’s outputs are copied into B or shared via files, prompt-like content could steer B. The pair lacks a documented shared channel, so this is inferred rather than observed.
conditions: IF A’s generated text is pasted into B’s browser-driven workflow
IF the pair is connected through a shared file or message channel
mitigations: Disable copy-paste of untrusted A output into B
Add a provenance label to A outputs before B consumes them
Review B prompts for instruction delimiters
Use a manual approval step before B acts on A text

B_data_leakage.rationale: A is local-only on network egress, but B has broad egress and handles sensitive classes including financial reports, logs, and execution traces. If the pair shares a workspace or secrets, B can transmit those materials to third-party APIs; A does not offset that risk. The exact shared path is undocumented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF A and B share files, logs, or secrets in the same workspace
IF B sends those materials through OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, DeepSeek, or Kaggle APIs
mitigations: Keep A and B in separate workspaces
Remove secrets from any shared directory
Restrict B API keys to least privilege
Rotate exposed keys after any shared-run test
requires-engineering: add per-agent data-loss prevention

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A’s write surfaces are undocumented, while B writes to log/ and supports multiple instances. If both touch the same directory or shared mutable resource, concurrent writes can corrupt outputs or logs. Because A’s write capability is not explicit, this is an uncertainty-driven medium rather than high.
conditions: IF A is configured with any filesystem write path overlapping B’s log/ directory
IF both agents write to the same mutable resource without locking
mitigations: Place each agent in a separate directory
Disable concurrent runs against shared files
Snapshot logs before B writes
Check for overlapping paths in the launcher
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: B’s research automation can treat upstream text as input, and A is an agent repository that may emit generated guidance or code-like content. If B consumes A output without verification, errors can cascade into research artifacts or actions. The pairwise handoff is not documented, so the risk is inferred and kept at medium.
conditions: IF B ingests A-produced text as authoritative input
IF B executes downstream steps without a verification gate
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A output
Add a validation step for citations and facts
Limit B to read-only analysis on A outputs
Log provenance for every A-to-B handoff

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly touches financial reports, logs, execution traces, and secrets, while A’s compliance posture is undocumented. If A and B are run under different residency or retention rules, shared handling of those classes can create policy mismatch. Because A lacks explicit compliance fields, the uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF A and B process the same regulated dataset under different retention or residency rules
IF B stores logs or traces containing restricted data outside approved policy
mitigations: Separate regulated data from general prompts
Confirm retention settings for B logs
Avoid placing secrets in shared folders
Document residency requirements before deployment
requires-engineering: align both agents to one compliance boundary
